title: Files and where programming is heading
subtitle: Variables vanish when the program ends; files remember. Then a glance at how programming grew up.

sections.title: Why files
sections.body: Variables live in RAM and disappear at exit. A file stores data on disk as a stream of bytes. Text files hold characters (readable, line-oriented); binary files hold raw bytes (compact, fast, not human-readable).

questions.prompt: Binary files differ from text files in that they…

choices.text: Store raw bytes, not character lines.

sections.title: The file lifecycle
sections.body: FILE *f = fopen("data.txt", "r"); returns a pointer, or NULL if opening fails — always check. Modes: r read, w write (truncates!), a append, r+ read/write; add b for binary. Then use fprintf/fscanf (formatted), fgets/fputs (lines), fread/fwrite (blocks), and finally fclose(f) so buffered data is flushed.

questions.prompt: Opening an existing file with mode “w” will…

figures.caption: Figure 9.2.1 — writing a file
figures.note: Data sits in a buffer until fclose or a flush.

sections.title: Reading until the end
sections.body: Read in a loop until the function reports end of file: while (fscanf(f, "%d", &x) == 1) stops when a value could not be read. Checking feof before reading causes the classic “last line processed twice” bug.

worked.why: A file holds 5 numbers: 4 6 8 2 10. Read and sum.

choices.text: The return value of the read function.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: It says whether a value was obtained.

problems.prompt: A binary file stores 250 records of 24 bytes each. File size?

sections.title: Random access
sections.body: fseek(f, offset, SEEK_SET) moves the position; ftell reports it. With fixed-size records, record n starts at byte n × size, so any record can be read without scanning the rest.

questions.prompt: Records are 32 bytes. Record 10 (counting from 0) starts at byte…

sections.title: Paradigms
sections.body: Procedural (C): a program is functions acting on data. Object-oriented (C++, Java, Python): data and the functions that act on it are bundled in classes. Functional: programs are compositions of pure functions. Modern languages mix them.

questions.prompt: The main idea of object-oriented programming is to…

choices.text: Bundle data with the operations on it.

figures.caption: Figure 10.1.1 — procedural → OOP
figures.note: Data and behaviour move together in OOP.

sections.title: Recent trends
sections.body: Memory-safe languages (Rust), scripting for data and AI (Python), web and mobile (JavaScript/Kotlin), WebAssembly, AI coding assistants, open-source libraries and version control as everyday tools. C remains the language of operating systems, embedded devices and compilers — learning it teaches how the machine really works.

questions.prompt: C is still taught first because it…

choices.text: Shows how memory, pointers and the machine really work.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Everything else is built on those ideas.
